gao-gaoreports-gao-08-148r: GAO wrote Congress in 2007 with an honest shrug: nobody could say if the 2005 bankruptcy rewrite hurt child support. The data to run a real study just did not exist. The letter is a rare official admission of a blind spot — Congress changed the rules for broke parents, then built no way to see how kids fared.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-78r: Written in 2007 as the housing crisis gathered force, this Government Accountability Office correspondence compiles information on default and foreclosure trends for home mortgages, plus the economic developments driving them. GAO lays out the data Congress needed to grasp the scale of the mortgage meltdown. The report reads as an early official chronicle of the collapse that would soon engulf the financial system.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1048r: A 2007 Government Accountability Office correspondence urging the Defense Department to give Congress and the public monthly data on enemy-initiated attacks in Iraq — on time. GAO argued that timely, consistent casualty and attack figures were essential for judging the war's progress. The letter captures the fight over war information: the Pentagon's reluctance to release data versus the public's right to know.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1088r: A 2007 Government Accountability Office correspondence on the Space Based Infrared System High program and its alternative — the satellites meant to detect missile launches. GAO examines the troubled program's status and the backup options. The report captures a moment in one of the Pentagon's most famously over-budget space programs, weighing whether to persist or pivot.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1148r: Payday lenders circling the barracks drew Congress's eye in 2007 — and GAO's letter grades the Pentagon's report on the predators. The findings say the report hit its assigned topics but leaned thin on proof for some claims. Protecting troops from debt traps, GAO implies, needs harder evidence than this.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1138r: Counting Guardsmen proved tricky in 2007 — GAO's letter says the Air National Guard had tightened its personnel numbers, with work left to do. The findings grade the reliability of the headcounts behind the force. In the Guard, the letter implies, you cannot deploy what you cannot count.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-878r: The home-loan banks' new stock rule was too fresh to judge in 2007 — GAO's letter says the impact on affordable housing could not yet be told. The findings counsel patience with the verdict. The letter's caution: do not grade the harvest before the planting.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-928r: Air-traffic modernization got its Q&A in 2007 — GAO's letter answers Congress's follow-ups from the hearing on the control system's future. The responses fill the gaps the testimony left open. The findings keep the modernization debate supplied with facts instead of slogans.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-918r: The next-gen air system faced its grilling in 2007 — GAO's letter answers the hearing's leftover questions on the JPDO blueprint. The responses supply the missing detail on costs and timing. The findings feed the long debate over rebuilding the nation's skies.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-768r: Stretching federal housing dollars was the theme in 2007 — GAO's letter explores leveraging public money for homes, blocks, and jobs. The findings showcase the multiplier game in action. The letter's pitch: make each federal dollar recruit private ones to the cause.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-298r: The Interior Department's cost math got a look in 2007 — GAO's letter reviews its managerial accounting habits across the agency. The findings test whether the land-and-parks agency truly knew its costs. The letter's nudge is gentle but firm: honest numbers make honest managers, and taxpayers deserve both.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-908r: New Orleans' pumps got a procurement probe in 2007 — GAO's letter examines the Corps' buying of drainage-canal pumping systems. The findings test the post-Katrina deals. The letter's stakes: the pumps that keep a city dry must be bought right.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-688r: Fuel-price swings were whipsawing the Pentagon's budget in 2007 — GAO's letter reviews how the department planned for the volatility. The findings test the hedging math in detail. The letter's question: was the war machine really budgeting for the pump price?
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-568r: The VA's job-rehab contracting was improving in 2007 — GAO's letter says managing the service deals had gotten better, with real challenges left. The findings credit the gains while listing the gaps. The letter's theme: wounded veterans deserve well-run help, not well-meant chaos.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-668r: Jewish war veterans' books got the audit in 2007 — GAO's letter reviews the organization's financial statements for the year. The findings give the formal opinion for the record. The letter shows every chartered cause, however honored, faces the same ledger check.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-318r: The whistleblower office's case system needed discipline in 2007, and GAO's letter says structured life-cycle practices were required. The findings demand the methodology. The letter's point: the office protecting truth-tellers should track its own cases properly. The truth-tellers' office had to mind its own files.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-328r: The learned societies' books got audited in 2007, and GAO's letter reviews the American Council of Learned Societies' financial statements. The findings give the formal opinion. The letter proves the scholars' ledgers get the same scrutiny as the soldiers'. The ivory tower got its audit.
